decision: gitloop is a pure-TypeScript reframe of issue #1's Python design: Node 22 LTS (pinned via .nvmrc), pnpm, Vitest, tsx, strict tsc; notifier and the three MCP tools in TS; the post-push git hook is a thin shell stub with no pipeline logic. Repo is a standalone git repo, remote daax-dev/gitloop.
rationale: Operator directive: pure-TypeScript tool. git requires an executable hook script, the only non-TS artifact. Standalone repo matches peer src/* subprojects (each its own repo; dx ignores src/).
alternatives: Keep the issue's Python Flask notifier + Python MCP (rejected: operator wants TS); hook as a Node shebang script (deferred: shell stub execing Node is simpler/portable); keep gitloop inside the dx repo (rejected: peers are separate repos).

decision: Tag-push events reach the tag-notifier via git's pre-push client hook (fire-and-forget HTTP POST), not a post-push hook. OBJECTIVE.md/PRD reference to .git/hooks/post-push is corrected: git has no client-side post-push hook.
rationale: Operator decision. githooks(5) defines pre-push as the only push-time client hook; payload (local ref, local sha, remote ref, remote sha) arrives on stdin. Fire-and-forget keeps git push native and avoids blocking on the notifier.
alternatives: post-receive on a shared bare repo (rejected: adds bare-repo topology setup); explicit gitloop push wrapper (rejected: loses native git push); notifier polling for-each-ref (rejected: least event-driven). Accepted risk: notify can fire before a push that subsequently fails.

decision: No CI/test gate on the test-complete transition. Validation is worker-driven: the receiving worker performs testing/review; on failure it retags the task backward with a version increment (rejection loop-back). advance_task does not enforce a passing test run.
rationale: Operator decision; resolves OBJECTIVE open question 1. CI is explicitly out of scope. Determinism is preserved because the loop-back is itself a tag transition verifiable from git state.
alternatives: Require local test evidence artifact before test-complete (rejected: re-introduces a gate where the next worker's validation already covers correctness).

decision: The pipeline is config-driven: ordered steps are defined in a gitloop pipeline config, not hardcoded to the six OBJECTIVE steps. Steps can be added/renamed. Each step may optionally require a per-step completion markdown artifact (e.g. review.md) committed to git before that step's tag is legal. Resolves OBJECTIVE open question 3, generalized beyond review.md.
rationale: Operator decision. Generalizing the review.md gate to any step keeps advance_task's artifact-requirement logic uniform and lets operators tailor the pipeline. The six OBJECTIVE steps ship as the default config.
alternatives: Hardcode six steps with a review.md-only gate (rejected: operator wants add/rename steps); no artifact gate at all (rejected: operator wants per-step gate option).

decision: Worker claim atomicity is enforced by pushing a claim tag to the shared remote; the remote ref update is atomic and rejects a duplicate, so the losing worker fails cleanly. No filesystem lock or state outside git.
rationale: Operator decision; resolves the claim-race design. git ref updates on push are atomic per-ref, giving a compare-and-swap primitive without an external lock, preserving the no-state-outside-git invariant.
alternatives: Local lockfile/advisory lock (rejected: introduces state outside git, violates the core invariant).
